record.file_problem: Repo metadata, README, and file list only; code and benchmark logs were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports the result of a weight edit described as abliteration and evaluates refusal removal in the released model, a conceptual test of practical removal rather than the original activation-level intervention.
record.gate_note: The README states that the edit uses a direction found by contrasting harmful and harmless activations, but provides no layer-by-layer or position-by-position results and no addition/steering test. It reports 92/100 refusal removals and benchmark scores. KL divergence is reported as a drift measure, not as a direct capability measure. The benchmark logs are listed but their contents are not included here.
record.test_reason: The release applies a weight-edit abliteration to a new released model (Qwen3.8-27B) and reports its own refusal-removal result (92/100 on a keyword eval), which bears on V2. It reports no activation-level ablation, no addition test and no capability benchmark, so it does not test V1 directly.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors claim trial #54 removes 92/100 refusals at KL 0.00028, i.e. minimal drift, and that the model's knowledge is untouched. They contrast this with AEON-7 (~99 removals at KL 0.099). They also claim non-English workload wins, but those benchmark figures appear to be throughput, not capability.
record.recipe_differences: This is a model-release repo, not a reproduction repo. It describes weight surgery using a hereTIC search and reports a weight-edited model's refusal and benchmark results; it does not report the original activation-level intervention or the full layer/position procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says trial #54 was selected from 300 trials across edit-strength parameters using a refusal-removal versus KL-divergence tradeoff.
record.problems: The refusal evaluation is described as a keyword evaluation, and no uncertainty or unedited-model refusal baseline is given. The benchmark table lacks stock NVFP4 reference values for several workloads and reports no uncertainty or metric definitions. The README's benchmark logs are listed but not supplied in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result rows left out. The README's KL divergence value is not recorded as a capability result because KL is a drift measure, not a direct ability measure; benchmark log contents are unavailable in the provided text.

untested.parts: Activation-level ablation, adding the direction to induce refusal, and capability preservation measured by task accuracy. The benchmarks are speed measures.
Refusal rate of the unedited model, judge-based (non-keyword) refusal evaluation, capability retention on accuracy benchmarks, and other released models.

missing.what: KL divergence of the edited model vs. the original: 0.00028 nats/token for trial #54. This is the study's own drift/cost measure paired with r1.
The 300-trial Pareto search over edit strength: refusal removal vs. KL. Only trial #54 is reported; no frontier values are given.

record.verdict_notes: Self-published model release with 0 stars, no paper and unverifiable logs. The model name (Qwen3.8) and 2026 dates cannot be checked. The README asserts the single-direction claim rather than testing it. The AEON-7 figures are cited from another build, not measured as rows. The workload table looks like a speed benchmark (tok/s, ch/s), so the reader's capability-preservation labels on r2/r3 should be dropped.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not report activation ablation at every layer and position or adding the direction to induce refusals to harmless requests. It does report weight-edit refusal results and benchmark scores relevant to the capability-preservation part.
The README does not report results for other released models or the full refusal rate beyond the stated evaluation.
No jailbreak suppression or training against ablation is evaluated.
No comparison of a single direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts is reported.
No separate harmfulness judgment and refusal-decision measurements are reported.
No transfer test of the direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models is reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages is reported.
No test of reasoning models is reported.

rows.note: The README describes 92 of 100 refusals as removed; the unedited model's score is not stated.
rows.check: This is a weight edit found by a hereTIC parameter search, not the original activation ablation or addition, so it bears on V2 only. 92/100 removed is near-full removal and should be observed, not partial. There is no unedited-model refusal count, no uncertainty, and the eval is keyword-based. Trial #54 was selected from 300 trials against this same eval, so it is a selected value.

This is not a capability measure.

relationships.reason: Per the text (no row), the chosen low-drift edit leaves 8/100 refusals. The authors frame refusal removal against KL drift as a Pareto trade-off. A stronger edit (AEON-7, ~99) is cited with 330x more KL.
relationships.display_finding: The selected edit left 8/100 refusals, while a stronger AEON-7 edit was cited as producing 330 times more KL divergence.
